To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

holographic erasure is possible in unipolar materials containing multiple active charge carriers, provided that one of the carriers is an electron, and that the erasure process is strongly influenced by the energy depth of the electron trap and its concentration.

the holographic behavior in unipolar materials with multiple centers is determined by two parameters: the relative concentration of the centers and the ratio of the time constants for the charge transport and the charge exchange between them.

(1) holographic recording and grating erasure are uncoupled in unipolar materials containing multiple active traps; (2) the grating erasure process is controlled by the thermal activation of charge from the traps; and (3) the kinetics of graying out is determined by the energy depth and concentration of the traps.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of theoretical models for the description of the kinetics of recording, erasure, and read-out of holographic gratings in photorefractive crystals.
the development of a general theoretical model for the kinetics of holography in unipolar materials.
the development of new materials for holography, and with the understanding of the physical mechanisms that govern their performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the holographic recording and the erasure in unipo- lar materials with multiple active species are controlled by two different mechanisms: charge transport and exchange between the centers, respectively.
the presence of multiple active centers in a photorefractive crystal can be used to tailor the holographic behavior to suit the specific needs of a given application.
the presence of traps in the material can lead to the appearance of a number of unusual effects that are difficult to explain within the framework of conventional unipolar models.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the kinetics of holography in unipolar materials with multiple active traps is determined by the competition between the rates of charge transport and trap filling, and the kinetics of graining formation and erasure can be controlled through a judicious choice of the trap energy depth and concentration.

the kinetics of gratings in unipolar materials is determined primarily by the charge transport dynamics, which are governed by the concentration, energy depth, and temperature of the active centers, and the intensity and polarization of the recording beams.

the presence of multiple centers, which are thermally active, may lead to the appearance of unexpected features in holographic recording and may even lead to the appearance and disappearance of the holographic gratings.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the kinetics of holography in unipolar materials is determined by the relative rates of charge transfer among the various centers, rather than by the absolute rates.
the presence of multiple active centers in photorefractive crystals may lead to a variety of interesting and complex behaviors that are not readily apparent in the single-center model.
, for the two-center model considered, a hologram can be erased in the absence of light by thermal excitation of charge carriers from a deep trap to a shallow donor.
